description.value: We examined symptoms of emotional blunting in two groups of younger onset dementia (bvFTD and early-onset AD) and investigated their neuroanatomical correlates using tensor-based morphometry.

spans.text: In the current study, we used tensor-based morphometry (TBM) to examine the neuroanatomical correlates of symptoms of emotional blunting on the SEB in patients with bvFTD and AD.

description.value: The current study included 25 patients (11 diagnosed with bvFTD and 14 with early-onset AD), who were recruited from the Neurobehavior Clinic at UCLA.

spans.text: The current study included 25 patients (11 diagnosed with bvFTD and 14 with early-onset AD), ranging in age from 42 to 76, who were recruited from the Neurobehavior Clinic at UCLA.

definition.value: The bvFTD group exhibited significantly smaller brain volume than the AD patients in the bilateral frontal lobes.

spans.text: Patients with bvFTD can exhibit variable presentations of the disease, including those with more positive symptoms such as disinhibited behavior, impulsivity and loss of social decorum, as well as those who exhibit more negative symptoms such as apathy, emotional blunting and lack of initiative.

value: The bvFTD group exhibited significantly smaller brain volume than the AD patients in the bilateral frontal lobes.
Although the bvFTD group exhibited more frontal atrophy overall, their symptoms of emotional blunting were most strongly correlated with the right anterior temporal lobe.

definition.value: The AD group demonstrated significantly smaller brain volume than the bvFTD group in the bilateral temporal lobes and left parietal region.

value: The AD group demonstrated significantly smaller brain volume than the bvFTD group in the bilateral temporal lobes, including the hippocampus, as well as the left parietal region.

spans.text: an observer rating scale with 16 items each assessed on a three-point scale (0 = “condition absent,” 1 = “slightly present or doubtful,” 2 = “clearly present”). Items assess symptoms across 3 domains: affect, behavior, and thought content.

Symptoms of emotional blunting were rated by the same examiner using the Scale for Emotional Blunting (SEB; [8]), an observer rating scale with 16 items each assessed on a three-point scale (0 = “condition absent,” 1 = “slightly present or doubtful,” 2 = “clearly present”).
